line: Fuel guy wants cash now. Up front. Cash. Twelve years I've paid that man on time.
Mornin', rookie. Easy day. Anguilla and back, and I'm coming with you. Don't look at me like that.
You keep looking back at the box. It's a box. Probably nothing. Probably.
where: Ch 1 The Extra Box · in flight (climb)

line: Unclench, man. You land, you taxi, you smile at the man. That's it.
where: Ch 1 The Extra Box · in flight (descent)

line: Same friend. One bag. Anguilla to Nevis, five hundred in your pocket. And rookie? Don't open it.
Four hundred grand behind your seat. If somebody stops you, what's the story? You don't have a story.
Coast Guard Dash 8, low level, crossing west of Saba.
The Dash 8 passes high and never looks your way.
where: Ch 2 Cash Run · flight order ok

line: You hesitated. The Dash 8 banks toward you for a closer look, then carries on.
where: Ch 2 Cash Run · flight order fail

line: Nevis traffic, be advised, police vehicle on the apron.
It's fish, man. Fish. Bring them home and don't go making friends.
Ease off, rookie. Customs swaps at four. Old man goes home, new boy waves us in. Kill some time.
where: Ch 3 The Ramp Check · in flight (cruise)

line: You land at five past four. The new officer barely looks up.
where: Ch 3 The Ramp Check · flight order ok

line: You land at ten to four. The old officer is still on, and he remembers your face.
where: Ch 3 The Ramp Check · flight order fail

line: Coral Wing, after landing, customs requests you park at the main apron.
where: Ch 3 The Ramp Check · in flight (descent)

line: Hangar first. Two minutes. Breathe, eh?
where: Ch 3 The Ramp Check · in flight (final)

line: So you're Dez's pilot. He says you have calm hands. I'd like to see them.
Be nice to this one. I mean it. Real nice.
Castillo is watching your hands. Not the instruments. Your hands.
Humor me. A steep turn. Forty-five degrees, all the way around. I like to know what I'm paying for.
You roll out on your heading. Castillo nods once. Good.
where: Ch 4 The Offer · flight order ok

line: Castillo watches you wobble through it and says nothing.
where: Ch 4 The Offer · flight order fail

line: Your jet training is paid for. $22,000 is in your account. Book the checkride. Don't make me wait.
where: Ch 4 The Offer · after the flight

line: Lionel Hartwell. My foundation owns her. On paper, anyway. Mateo says you're the best he's found, and Mateo is very hard to please.
where: Ch 5 Keys to the Jet · prologue

line: Nine bags. Don't count them. Money isn't a crime, my friend. Not until somebody asks where it came from.
where: Ch 5 Keys to the Jet · prologue

line: Flight level two zero zero, a million dollars in the back. You keep waiting to feel scared.
where: Ch 5 Keys to the Jet · in flight (climb)

line: How does she fly? Good. Get used to it.
where: Ch 5 Keys to the Jet · in flight (cruise)

line: Unknown aircraft squawking 4521, say your destination and souls on board.
where: Ch 5 Keys to the Jet · in flight (cruise)

line: No stops. No radio. They paid for quiet.
The boy's breathing is getting worse. You can feel them all looking at you.
The boy is wheezing hard. There's an oxygen bottle in the emergency kit, and Castillo's rule is no stops, no favors.
Arnaud won't stop talking about his daughter. You turn the volume up.
Is my lawyer comfortable? Good. See that he arrives.
Arnaud is asleep. His hard drive is sticking out of his jacket pocket.
Nobody will fly in this. That's the point. Name a number. I'll double it.
You're the pilot? I'm Tico, I do the bags. One day I'm gonna fly one of these, boss, for real, you watch.
Coast Guard six five zero four, San Juan, returning to base due to weather.
where: Ch 8 Into the Storm · in flight (climb)

line: Look around. Nobody else up there. That's why I pay you.
where: Ch 8 Into the Storm · in flight (cruise)

line: Rain hammering the windscreen and you're grinning like an idiot.
where: Ch 8 Into the Storm · in flight (descent)

line: Punta Cana is reporting a thunderstorm over the field.
where: Ch 8 Into the Storm · in flight (cruise)

line: The cell drifts off. Late, but every bag is dry.
where: Ch 8 Into the Storm · flight order ok

line: You landed in the tail of the storm. Two bags are soaked through.
where: Ch 8 Into the Storm · flight order fail

line: Easy run. You're already spending the money in your head.
Sealed case behind the seat. Your stomach hasn't felt like this since the Cessna.
You're not a delivery boy anymore. Welcome to the family business.
Boss! Boss. They put me on your crew. Your crew! I called my mom already.
Fourteen hundred pounds a trip. A 737 freighter takes forty thousand. You run the numbers again. And again.
A text from an unknown number: We know who you are. You delete it, and then you check your mirrors all the way down.
Nice jet. Text me every tail number on that ramp. Every one.
Boss, can I sit up front? One minute. I just wanna see it. I won't touch nothing.
Relax, boss, nobody's gonna touch the jet. Who'd even try that?
Traffic, two o'clock, same altitude, no transponder.
The dark jet can't keep up. It peels off toward the coast.
where: Ch 11 The Medinas · flight order ok

line: They sit on your wing all the way down. Somebody was taking photos.
where: Ch 11 The Medinas · flight order fail

line: Someone on your crew talks to the DEA. I think it's the boy. Tico.
Fly him to Grand Cayman. Some friends will meet him. To talk. Only to talk.
Boss. Remember when you let me sit up front? Ten minutes. Best ten minutes I ever had.
where: Ch 12 The Rat · prologue (depends on choices)

line: Tico won't look at you. He flew the storm with you. He wanted to be a pilot.
Dez knew what this was. My lawyer rides with you. And please, no tears in my airplane.
Castillo's lawyer finally looks up from Dez's file. How much is Dez worth to you?
Dez won't talk. He's covering for someone. If it's you, this is your window.
Thinking about Dez? Don't. Sentiment is expensive.
She works for me, not for Dez. Remember that when she starts asking questions.
Don't. I don't want the speech. Take me up. Grand Case, the way you used to fly it when you were scared of everything.
Mari hasn't said anything since takeoff. She's looking at the water.
I'll take the jump seat, if that's all right. I have something for you, and I've rather gone off telephones.
Your first airliner. A hundred and fifty thousand pounds, and it does what you tell it.
My foundation has been laundering Mateo's money for years. I built it to save a reef, you know. A reef. I want out.
If I hand you the ledgers he'll know it was me. So I'd like a seat on a plane out. Somewhere with no extradition and decent tea.
Lovely airline. I'll take half.
An airline. Ambitious. I want every invoice and every tail number.
Eighteen tons a night, and your name on the tail.
Half. We'll talk on the ground.
Caribe one, Tocumen ground. Customs requests you taxi to remote stand seven.
My friend! Forget the airline business. I booked you a run myself. Like the old days.
My lawyer says you had a lot to say about Dez. It doesn't matter. We're friends.
where: Ch 17 The Setup · prologue (depends on choices)

line: Castillo hasn't been this nice to you in months. That's what bothers you.
Something's off about this run. You can't put your finger on it.
Rookie. Rookie, it's me. Castillo sold you, man. Medinas on the cargo ramp. Park by the terminal and walk out with the tourists. Go.
Listen to me. Not the cargo ramp. Castillo sold you to the Medinas. Park at the terminal and walk out with the tourists.
Wiretap just lit up. Castillo sold you to the Medinas. Stay off the cargo ramp. I mean it.
It's Tico. You let me run, so now I owe you. Castillo sold you to the Medinas, boss. Cargo ramp. Don't go there.
Eighty tons. I counted every pallet twice. Bring her home, partner.
Four engines, eighty tons. Two years ago a box in a Cessna made you sweat.
A 747. Look at you. Don't forget whose money taught you to fly.
Trucks are here. Rain's coming. Don't make me wait in it.
Heavy aircraft, unidentified, this is the U.S. Coast Guard on guard. Identify yourself.
Down in the radar clutter. The Coast Guard loses you over the water.
They tracked you all the way in.
There's a seat at the table for you, amigo. Bring the big airplane. These people love a big airplane.
A table of suppliers in Cancún. Remember the faces.
Somewhere down there, a table full of people is looking up.
Before you land, give them a show. Low pass, right down the runway. I want them to feel four engines in their teeth.
Four engines at two hundred feet. Every phone at the table is pointed at you.
where: Ch 19 The Table · flight order ok

line: You never got low enough. Medina's men are laughing at the table.
where: Ch 19 The Table · flight order fail

line: I'll ride with you, if you don't mind. One last flight. To make peace.
We're in position. Whatever you're planning, don't.
where: Ch 20 The Last Run · prologue (depends on choices)

line: Castillo is pretending to sleep in the jump seat. An hour to Miami. An hour to make up your mind.
where: Ch 20 The Last Run · in flight (cruise)

line: Miami's ready for you. So are we. Don't be clever.
where: Ch 20 The Last Run · in flight (cruise)

line: I don't pay for wreckage. Get yourself together and do it again. Properly.
